topic: Deletion-rank equilibrium-effect frontier for source-minimal cyclic latent LiNG models. Given a normalized full-row-rank overcomplete ICA representation X=C epsilon with independent moment-determinate non-Gaussian sources and no zero or proportional columns, range over every latent cyclic SCM completion with exactly those source directions, zero structural diagonal, invertible observational and postintervention systems, and no stability assumption. For ordered observed x!=y, prove the sharp equilibrium-effect set is {C_yj/C_xj: C_xj!=0 and rank(C_{-x,-j})=p-1}; construct a full same-law completion for every admissible j, characterize identification iff the set is a singleton, return two exact SCMs otherwise, and certify all values in O(n^4) arithmetic operations. For iid samples on a common-cumulant-order subclass with fixed moment, tensor-separation, minor, and denominator margins, derive the OICA inverse and simultaneous confidence union with uniform coverage and root-N Hausdorff uncertainty. Use Dai et al. 2026 and Tramontano et al. as anchors and the 14-stock HSI equivalence class as the consumer; graphical irreducibility without source minimality is explicitly excluded.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp set of ordered-pair hard-intervention equilibrium effects over all source-minimal cyclic latent LiNG completions compatible with one fixed overcomplete-ICA observational law.

source_refs.claim: Characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence for latent-variable cyclic LiNG models, but not numerical intervention effects within the completion fiber of one fixed law.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Gives complete graphical criteria for direct and total causal-effect identification in latent-variable acyclic LiNGAM and identifies cyclic effect criteria as an open extension.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Provides only partial cyclic identification results, shows a reciprocal two-cycle ambiguity, and explicitly leaves complete cyclic characterization for future work.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Mathias Drton, Jalal Etesami

source_refs.claim: Shows that cyclic SCMs require explicit observational and interventional solvability conditions.
source_refs.author: Stephan Bongers, Patrick Forré, Jonas Peters, Joris M. Mooij

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dai et al. compare graph-indexed distribution families after graphical irreducibility, whereas a fixed observed law supplies numerical source directions and asks which source assignments admit zero-diagonal, observationally invertible, and postintervention-invertible completions. Tramontano et al.'s complete effect arguments use acyclicity, and their cyclic results do not enter the arbitrary-latent same-law fiber. The missing step is an algebraic feasibility characterization tying a treatment-loaded source direction to a full source-minimal completion while preserving the exact mixing law; targeted searches found no result with this fixed-law scope and conclusion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient deletion-rank characterization of the attainable finite effect set, with exact same-law SCM witnesses for every value, a singleton criterion, two countermodels when nonidentified, and a polynomial-time certification algorithm.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction centers the causal-effect query rather than whole-graph recovery and separates known-graph from unknown-graph ambiguity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding destroys ordinary LiNGAM point identification -> OICA still exposes source directions and compatible assignments -> acyclic criteria identify invariant effects -> characterize the equilibrium-effect set inside a fixed cyclic same-law fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Use edge-rank constraints, children bases, and perfect matchings to encode compatible latent cyclic structures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The fixed-law feasibility test is likewise rank-and-matching based, but must localize the argument to numerical deletion minors and source assignments.

method_exemplars.technique: Normalize and permute ICA components to enumerate cyclic LiNG SEMs compatible with an observational distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational same-distribution cyclic-LiNG construction; the destination adds overcomplete latent sources and effect invariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive efficient-score estimation and root-N asymptotic linearity for an ICA mixing matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Away from zero denominators and rank boundaries, effect coordinates are smooth ratios of recovered source directions, although overcompleteness and set-valued output require new work.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop uniform inference for the finite equilibrium-effect frontier when overcomplete mixing directions, deletion-rank membership, and ratio denominators are estimated from iid samples.

source_refs.claim: Gives an if-and-only-if OICA identifiability characterization and a coupled matrix-tensor recovery algorithm, but not confidence regions for downstream set-valued causal effects.
source_refs.author: Kexin Wang, Anna Seigal

source_refs.claim: Uses higher-order cumulants for closed-form OICA recovery in structured latent LiNGAM cases, but does not give simultaneous uncertainty for a rank-selected causal effect set.
source_refs.author: Ruichu Cai, Zhiyi Huang, Wei Chen, Zhifeng Hao, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Uses estimated OICA mixing matrices and rank tests without a uniform limit law for effect-set endpoints or rank-selection errors.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Mixing-direction estimation alone does not provide coverage for the frontier: labels and scales must be aligned, deletion-rank membership is discontinuous, and ratios are nonregular near vanishing treatment loadings. Existing OICA work supplies population identification, recovery algorithms, or component-error bounds, but the scan found no simultaneous confidence union with uniform coverage over explicit tensor-separation, minor, and denominator margins and no Hausdorff limit theorem for the induced finite causal set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit cumulant-tensor OICA inverse on a separated iid subclass, a uniform root-N expansion for all retained ratios, a simultaneous confidence union with uniform coverage, and a root-N Hausdorff error bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It moves from an exact OICA identifiability question to an implementable coupled matrix-tensor recovery method.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ordinary ICA excludes more sources than observations -> algebraic geometry restores OICA identifiability -> coupled decompositions recover source directions -> quantify uncertainty for the causal set computed from those directions.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover mixing directions through linear spaces of rank-one symmetric matrices and coupled matrix-tensor decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The effect-frontier estimator requires exactly these normalized overcomplete source directions.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine tensor concentration with perturbation analysis of rank-one component recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its moment-error-to-factor-error proof can be composed with deletion-minor and ratio perturbation bounds for Hausdorff control.

method_exemplars.technique: Use optimally weighted minimum distance for cumulant restrictions with asymptotic variance and bootstrap covariance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Away from separation failures, the proposed inverse is a smooth local solution of stacked cumulant restrictions.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend overcomplete source-direction recovery and simultaneous equilibrium-effect-set inference to weakly dependent financial time series so that the 14-stock Hong Kong illustration has a defensible sampling model.

source_refs.claim: Applies glvLiNG to 1,331 daily adjusted closing-price observations on 14 HSI constituents and returns an equivalence class of 19,008 graphs, without dependent-data effect-set inference.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Finds changing mechanisms and latent driving forces in Hong Kong stock returns, putting a fixed iid interpretation in tension with the application domain.
source_refs.author: Biwei Huang, Kun Zhang, Jiji Zhang, Joseph Ramsey, Ruben Sanchez-Romero, Clark Glymour, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: Proves consistency and root-T asymptotic normality for frequency-domain ICA with mutually independent but serially correlated sources in a square mixing model.
source_refs.author: Seonjoo Lee, Haipeng Shen, Young K. Truong

source_refs.excerpt: Finite-sample inference on a restricted domain, dependent-latent robustness ... remain open.
Heterogeneous decays, hidden labels, growing p, and sample inference for feedback mechanisms remain unresolved.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The HSI observations are a single daily financial series, so iid cumulant concentration and iid bootstrap calibration are not justified without a sampling model; related Hong Kong data also show mechanism changes. Existing dependent-time-series ICA limit theory is square and exploits source spectra, while the destination is overcomplete instantaneous direction recovery followed by discontinuous deletion-rank selection and a finite ratio set. The prior LiNGAM run independently records restricted-domain finite-sample and dependence robustness as open, while the Hawkes run's HAC theory excludes feedback. The first proof step that must change is the iid joint sample-cumulant CLT: it must become a uniform dependent-process cumulant CLT with a consistent long-run covariance estimator before tensor inversion and simultaneous set construction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A stationary weak-dependence or locally stationary theorem giving consistent overcomplete source recovery, HAC- or block-bootstrap simultaneous coverage for the equilibrium-effect set, root-T Hausdorff uncertainty, and an empirical certificate for tensor, minor, and denominator separation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Appendix D.5 supplies the exact 14-stock consumer, the latent cyclic equivalence class, and the empirical scale of the ambiguity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: HSI prices exhibit hidden common drivers -> glvLiNG returns 19,008 compatible latent cyclic graphs -> a query-specific effect frontier compresses that ambiguity -> daily dependence and possible nonstationarity require honest simultaneous uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Joint Whittle estimation of source spectra and the unmixing matrix, followed by score-Hessian sandwich asymptotics and plug-in covariance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves root-T ICA inference under serial correlation; the transfer must handle overcompleteness, cumulant recovery, and set-valued causal output.

method_exemplars.technique: Fit autoregressive dynamics and apply non-Gaussian ICA to innovations for contemporaneous identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Residualization is the first natural route to separate lag dependence from the instantaneous fixed-law mixing matrix.

method_exemplars.technique: Use time-indexed independent mechanism changes to diagnose nonstationarity and recover latent driving forces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A defensible HSI analysis must distinguish stationary dependence, where HAC inference applies, from changing mechanisms that invalidate one fixed mixing law.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a source-specific multi-order cumulant recovery and inference procedure when each non-Gaussian source has an informative cumulant order but no common order is nonzero and separating for every source.

source_refs.claim: Identifies OICA from the full distribution, leaving a gap between full-law identifiability and recovery from a single finite-order cumulant tensor.
source_refs.author: Kexin Wang, Anna Seigal

source_refs.claim: Recovers underdetermined mixtures through fourth-order cumulant simultaneous diagonalization, requiring that the chosen order reveal the components.
source_refs.author: Lieven De Lathauwer, Joséphine Castaing, Jean-François Cardoso

source_refs.claim: Jointly uses third- and fourth-order cumulants with asymptotic distributions for square ICA, but does not align arbitrary source-specific orders in an overcomplete decomposition.
source_refs.author: Joni Virta, Klaus Nordhausen, Hannu Oja

open_problems.why_unsolved: Moment determinacy and non-Gaussianity imply departure from Gaussianity somewhere but do not provide one fixed cumulant order at which every source coefficient is nonzero. A one-order tensor pencil can therefore omit legitimate columns, while separate decompositions at several orders create unresolved cross-order labels, scales, and collisions. Third-plus-fourth-order square-ICA methods demonstrate the principle but do not cover overcomplete source-specific orders or propagate adaptive order selection into causal-set inference; targeted searches found no general multi-order OICA inverse for this setting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive finite-order selection rule and coupled tensor-factorization map recovering all source directions under explicit heterogeneous-order separation, with a root-N limit law or finite-sample confidence guarantee for the induced equilibrium-effect set.

writing_exemplar.why: It foregrounds the distinction between exact OICA identifiability and an executable recovery algorithm.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full-law non-Gaussian information identifies overcomplete mixtures -> practical recovery uses finite tensor summaries -> one order can erase some sources -> build an adaptive multi-order inverse supporting effect-set inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert fourth-order cumulant slices into simultaneous diagonalization and off-diagonalization problems.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each informative order yields rank-one powers of the same directions, so its slice algebra is a building block for coupled cross-order factorization.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine third- and fourth-order cumulant estimating equations with root-N asymptotic variance calculations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already combines skewness and kurtosis information; the required advance is arbitrary orders, overcompleteness, and label alignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate cumulant-generating-function Hessians and recover overcomplete atoms through an SDP tolerant of noisy subspace estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Generating-function Hessians aggregate information beyond one fixed cumulant order and may align heterogeneous-order sources.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp joint fiber of several hard-intervention equilibrium effects under one common source-minimal cyclic LiNG completion, rather than taking a Cartesian product of scalar frontiers.

source_refs.claim: Derives possible joint-intervention effects and inference over acyclic no-hidden-variable equivalence classes, not latent cyclic fixed-law fibers.
source_refs.author: Preetam Nandy, Marloes H. Maathuis, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: Provides matching-based latent cyclic equivalence machinery but does not map fixed-law completions to joint intervention response matrices.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Characterizes ordered-pair effects in acyclic latent LiNGAM, not simultaneous interventions in cyclic same-law fibers.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.excerpt: record the finite set of direct-effect/source-label alternatives within a fixed arrow.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar ratio witnesses need not come from one common completion: coordinatewise constructions may use incompatible latent-row shears or source assignments. For a treatment block, replacing several equations produces a block-minor or Schur-complement functional, and candidate assignments are coupled by global matching, zero-diagonal constraints, and simultaneous postintervention invertibility. Joint-IDA supplies the destination vocabulary only for observed acyclic DAGs, while the prior reviewer specifically asks to retain the finite source-label alternatives. The first proof step must replace the one-row cofactor argument with a simultaneous completion theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient finite or semialgebraic characterization of all jointly attainable equilibrium response vectors or matrices, with common-law SCM witnesses, a singleton criterion, and an output-sensitive algorithm avoiding graph enumeration.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates joint interventions as a distinct target and separates possible-effect sets from point effects.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific interventions often manipulate several variables -> model ambiguity yields multiple compatible joint effects -> local computations can avoid full graph enumeration -> characterize the exact joint response set under latent cyclic source-assignment uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Use perfect matchings, edge ranks, and children bases to encode globally compatible source assignments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Several treatment equations require simultaneous source assignments, making global matching compatibility load-bearing.

method_exemplars.technique: Use recursive regression and modified Cholesky constructions for joint effects, with asymptotic variance and high-dimensional consistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its matrix-valued joint-effect parameter and joint uncertainty analysis are the closest inferential analogue after identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute distinct possible intervention effects from local equivalence information without enumerating every DAG.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination likewise needs a compressed representation of distinct compatible effects rather than all completions.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine exactly which deletion-rank-admissible equilibrium-effect ratios remain attainable after imposing observational and postintervention dynamical stability on source-minimal latent cyclic LiNG completions.

source_refs.claim: Enumerates cyclic LiNG observationally equivalent models in the causally sufficient case and gives sufficient conditions under which only one compatible SEM is stable.
source_refs.author: Gustavo Lacerda, Peter Spirtes, Joseph Ramsey, Patrik O. Hoyer

source_refs.claim: Characterizes arbitrary-latent cyclic equivalence under invertible linear systems without characterizing the stable subset of a fixed numerical fiber.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Separates solvability and unique solvability of cyclic SCMs from stronger dynamical interpretations.
source_refs.author: Stephan Bongers, Patrick Forré, Jonas Peters, Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.excerpt: state rho(I-D)<1 separately and re-check the converse within that narrower class.
The invariant nuisance is positive semidefinite in the standard BACKSHIFT layer.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Deletion rank certifies an algebraic completion but does not control the spectral radius of its structural matrix. The row shear used to realize a selected ratio can cross the unit spectral boundary even when the observational and intervened equation systems remain invertible, and observational stability need not imply postintervention stability. Lacerda et al. show that stability can prune square, causally sufficient cyclic candidates, while the prior BACKSHIFT reviewer warns that cycle-product normalization is not genuine spectral stability. The completion lemma must therefore preserve the relevant spectral inequalities or certify impossibility.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact formula or finite semialgebraic criterion for the stable effect subset, with a stable completion for every retained ratio, impossibility certificates for deleted ratios, and a decision algorithm for empty, singleton, and multiple stable fibers.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames stability as extra information that can shrink a cyclic observational equivalence class.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ICA identifies several cyclic SEMs with one observational law -> stability can rule out compatible SEMs -> uniqueness occurs in special square cases -> determine the exact stable equilibrium-effect subset with latent sources.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate ICA-compatible cyclic SEMs and filter them using stability conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly precedes stability-refined equivalence, but square permutations must be replaced by overcomplete source-minimal completion geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Traverse latent cyclic equivalence classes through constrained graph moves preserving edge-rank structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These moves can identify where stability fails to be invariant and organize the stable-witness search.

method_exemplars.technique: Use pseudo-maximum-likelihood ICA for structural VARs with consistency and asymptotic inference under non-Gaussian shocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A stability-refined empirical frontier needs uncertainty for mixing-derived effects and spectral constraints; SVAR ICA is the closest econometric template.

literature_map:
1. Dai, Albrecht, Spirtes, and Zhang (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.04780) characterize distributional equivalence for latent cyclic LiNG graphs using path ranks, edge ranks, children bases, and class traversal.
2. Their object is a graph-indexed family of observed laws after graphical irreducibility, not the numerical completion fiber of one fixed OICA law or its intervention-effect image.
3. Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (ICML 2024, arXiv:2406.02049) characterize direct and total effects for acyclic lvLiNGAM and name cyclic extension as open.
4. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (arXiv:2405.20856v2) give partial cyclic results, the reciprocal two-cycle ambiguity, and leave complete cyclic identification for future work.
5. Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer (UAI 2008, arXiv:1206.3273) establish square-ICA cyclic LiNG equivalence and show stability can sometimes select a compatible SEM.
6. Bongers, Forré, Peters, and Mooij (Annals of Statistics 2021, DOI 10.1214/21-AOS2064) show why cyclic interventions need explicit solvability conditions.
7. Hoyer et al. (IJAR 2008) and Salehkaleybar et al. (JMLR 2020) anchor latent LiNGAM through OICA but retain acyclicity and structural restrictions.
8. Wang and Seigal (Bernoulli 2026, DOI 10.3150/25-BEJ1929; arXiv:2401.14709) give an iff OICA identifiability criterion and coupled matrix-tensor recovery.
9. Podosinnikova et al. (AISTATS 2019, arXiv:1901.08334) use cumulant-generating-function Hessians and an SDP instead of one fixed high-order tensor.
10. Anandkumar, Ge, and Janzamin (COLT 2015, arXiv:1408.0553) give tensor concentration and overcomplete component recovery, but not causal set coverage.
11. Cai et al. (ICML 2023, arXiv:2305.19582) derive structured higher-cumulant OICA formulas; Tramontano et al. (ICML 2025, arXiv:2506.05202) use cumulants for special acyclic latent-effect designs.
12. Virta, Nordhausen, and Oja (arXiv:1505.02613) combine third and fourth cumulants with root-N theory for square ICA, leaving arbitrary source-specific orders and overcompleteness open.
13. Dai et al.'s HSI appendix uses 1,331 daily adjusted closing-price observations on 14 stocks and returns 19,008 compatible 16-vertex graphs, so iid coverage is not automatically defensible.
14. Lee, Shen, and Truong (JMVA 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.jmva.2020.104692) prove root-T square-ICA inference for serially correlated sources, while Huang et al. (JMLR 2020, arXiv:1903.01672) document changing mechanisms in Hong Kong returns.
15. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Bühlmann (Annals 2009) and Nandy, Maathuis, and Richardson (Annals 2017) represent possible single and joint effects over DAG classes; no located paper transfers this to source-minimal latent cyclic equilibrium effects.
